$comment: Shared input/expected vectors for VfDropdown. The TypeScript rules in dropdown/state.ts run every section; the PHP mirror in packages/razor/src/Support/DropdownState.php runs the sections a server can decide (listed in $serverRules) and deliberately has no method for the others - the menu walk, the arrow offset, the flip pair and the opening keys are browser decisions a server never makes. The contract of the reference at fd793696, quirks included: a disabled dropdown is never open whatever its disclosure says; aria-disabled is "true" or absent, never "false"; the variant is written through unvalidated; --top follows the computed placement; only bottom-end selects the end flip pair; the arrow offset is 0 on an axis missing either number; teleportTo false or null renders in place and anything that is not a string means body; the walk starts from -1, so ArrowUp from no item lands on the second to last. `null` in `teleportTo` is JSON null; an absent key is `undefined`. There is deliberately no vector for a focus move, a listener, the escape stack or a position: the rule set holds no state and runs no floating code.

resolveDropdownOpen.$why: A disabled dropdown is closed whatever the disclosure holds.

resolveDropdownTriggerState.$why: aria-disabled only ever "true"; aria-expanded follows the open predicate, so a disabled open disclosure announces false.

resolveDropdownMenuClasses.$why: The computed placement decides --top, whatever was requested.
The variant is not validated: an unknown one becomes a modifier no stylesheet selects.

resolveDropdownArrowClasses.$why: Anything not starting with top is bottom.

resolveDropdownFlipPlacements.$why: Only bottom-end selects the end pair.

resolveDropdownArrowOffset.$why: A missing base zeroes that axis only.

resolveDropdownTeleport.$why: Explicit null renders in place in Vue. Razor reads a null attribute as not given (its adapter convention) and spells this `false`, so the PHP mirror skips this one vector.
disableTeleport wins over a selector, which is still resolved.

resolveDropdownMenuNavigation.$why: From no item ArrowDown lands on the first.
From no item ArrowUp lands on the second to last: (-1 - 1 + 3) % 3.
Keys the menu leaves to the browser.
